anti_gaming: One active claim per contributor per bounty. A claim reserves the bounty for 7 days (T1-T2) or 14 days (T3+). It reopens after that without a progress update.

Staged release for T3+ code (spec, then implementation, then independent audit; econ-dex-proxy-analysis.md s3.6). The spec author holds first right to implement. The audit is never by the implementer.

Staged verification: cheap deterministic prechecks run first and a hard fail stops the pipeline before any model is called; then cheap-model triage, the strong validator, the full deterministic acceptance checks, and the human. The model judge is advisory only, and a judge failure means needs_human. No model, webhook or event can approve or pay (platform-plan.md D6).
Identity: ADR-36 login plus bountyPk binding. The same payee across multiple accounts in one window is flagged (platform-plan.md s4 step 3).
No self-review and no self-approval. Self-nominations for retro are allowed but flagged.
Ops and relayer pay is in arrears against on-chain tx hashes. Terp never pre-funds hot wallets beyond a short working balance (relayer plan RS3, RS4).
Content bounties pay for accuracy and completeness, never for likes, follows, views or posting volume. No price talk, no promises of returns (comms SPEC G3/G4).
Submissions are untrusted data. Instructions aimed at the judge (prompt injection) disqualify the submission and are logged (comms SPEC G9).
No splitting work to slip under a tier or governance threshold. Related claims by the same contributor are summed.
Security: responsible disclosure only. No testing against mainnet funds or other people's accounts. Public disclosure only after a fix ships or 90 days pass, whichever comes first.
Per-contributor cap: no more than 25% of a month's bounty budget to one payee without human sign-off naming the reason.
AI-assisted work is welcome and must be disclosed. It is judged by the same criteria.
